pages.title: Spent fuel and the pool
text: A discharged assembly keeps its decay heat: 315 kW at discharge for a 45 GWd/t assembly, 63 kW after an hour and 23 kW after a day. It waits in the spent fuel pool.

Build a lined box of Spent Fuel Pool Lining (outside 5 to 64 blocks wide and deep, 8 to 24 high) with one Spent Fuel Pool Controller and racks: exactly four rack blocks stacked on the floor make one rack of four assemblies, up to 2,048 racks (8,192 assemblies) in one pool. Fit a makeup port and the cooling ports. You run the cooling and supply the makeup water. Let it go and the water boils off and the fuel uncovers.

pages.title: The new fuel elevator
text: Stand a New Fuel Elevator on top of the rim of a formed pool wall, on a straight run. Its guide frame hangs down the inside of the wall under the water. Put an assembly in its hatch by right-click, hopper or pipe and the carriage takes it down, over the racks, into the first free cell.

It says why when it refuses: not on a pool, every cell taken, or under 1.5 m of water over the handle. RAISE COOLEST on its screen brings the coolest assembly back up. A hot one out of the water is a radiation source.

pages.title: The refuelling bridge
text: Fuel moves on a refuelling bridge, one assembly at a time and always under water. Build two parallel runs of Refuelling Rail over the open reactor and the pool, the cattle chute (a slot, see the page after Flood the well) between them, and a Refuelling Bridge Console beside a rail.

The bridge moves fuel only. The head, the dryer and the separators are lifted by the reactor building crane (the next pages). Instant refuelling by clicking the refuelling map is a server option, off by default.

pages.title: Lifting the shield plugs
text: The shield plug over the well comes off first. Cut it into pieces with the Plug Seam Marker: right-click a plug block near the edge for the cut. A groove marks the seam; click again to undo, sneak-click to clear a block.

Bolt exactly four Crane Anchors on the top of a piece, then press PLUG OFF in the crane console: the nearest rigged piece goes to clear floor. Over 125 t (a block is 2.4, 3.2 or 4.0 t by tier) it is refused: add a seam. PLUG ON puts the last piece back. The head will not lift with a plug over the well.

pages.title: Opening the vessel
text: The head does not come off with a button. Depressurise to 25 psig or less, stand a Stud Tensioner on the refuel floor beside the well, give it power and press DETENSION. The tool goes round the flange stud by stud, 4 seconds and 3,000 FE each: 296 seconds and 222,000 FE for 74 studs. The nuts come off; the studs stay in the flange.
After the crane has set the head back, RETENSION brings the studs to load, 6 seconds and 6,000 FE each. The vessel holds pressure only with every stud at load.

pages.title: The reactor building crane
text: The crane lifts the head, the dryer and the separators. Build two parallel runs of Crane Runway Rail high on opposite walls of the hall, up to 40 blocks apart, over the reactor, and a Crane Console beside a rail. Place a Head Stand on clear floor between the rails beside the well, as much room round it as the vessel is wide.
In the console, LIFT HEAD carries the head on its strongback to the stand. The head lifts only with every stud detensioned. If the rails are too low the console says how high to build them.

pages.title: Flood the well
text: With the head off, raise the water over the flange: your feed, condensate or RHR (LPCI) pumps, or a Cavity Fill Port. Nothing floods by itself.

The INFO tab's "Flooding the well" checklist marks each need PASS or FAIL and says where: the head off, the studs bare, a cavity seal (full blocks touching the vessel or one block off, all round), the well's wall closed up to the flange, water going in, and water leaving (into the drywell: no usable well; over the top: it is full).
A Cavity Drain Port lowers it again.

pages.title: The cavity fill port
text: Set a Cavity Fill Port in the well's wall or floor at or above the seal, its flange out of the well (place it looking out).

Pipe a pump's discharge to it (feed, condensate, RHR or core spray): the water goes straight into the well. Or pipe it through a Motor-Operated Water Valve to a Condensate Storage Tank higher than the water: open the valve and the tank fills the well by gravity, up to 1,500 kg/s. Right-click the port to see what its line is doing.

pages.title: The cattle chute
text: Cut a slot through the pool wall and the well wall in a row both share. Put Transfer Canal stacks in it from the rim down, facing the wall, a Canal Gate Plug stack in the pool-wall slot (the gate), and canal stacks between the walls. The slot's lowest block stands at least one block above the rack tops.

Flood the well to the pool's level, then pull the gate with the crane. Open, the pool, the canal and the well are one water: the higher side runs into the lower over the slot's floor. A gate in the canal holds them apart.

pages.title: Pulling a canal gate
text: A real canal gate is a steel plug the crane lifts out. Stack Canal Gate Plug blocks in a canal column from the rim down: the stack is one gate, and the canal is shut. Put a Gate Laydown Stand on the floor in the crane's reach.

Flood the well to the pool's level first: a gate is pulled only with both sides within 0.3 m. GATE OUT on the crane console hooks the eyes on its top and lays it on the stand; the pool, the canal and the well are then one water. GATE IN puts it back exactly.

pages.title: Dryer and separators out
text: With the head off and the vessel flooded to its flange, the crane lifts the dryer, then the separators. Place an Equipment Storage Pad for each on the floor of a pit of water between the rails and press DRYER OUT, then SEPS OUT, in the crane console.
Both come up out of the water, so the survey meter spikes; keep the pit full. To close up: SEPS IN, DRYER IN, then SET HEAD, and retension the studs. The head will not go on until both are back.

pages.title: Moving fuel with the bridge
text: The vessel head must be off, the well flooded and the dryer and separators out first (all with the crane). In the bridge console's map pick a core position and a rack cell, then TO POOL or TO CORE. A move takes about 50 seconds on the smallest plant.
The bridge will not lift an assembly higher than leaves 1.5 m of water over it unless you override. An assembly lifted out of the water makes the survey meter spike.
